# 0008. Art generated by script rather than hand-modelled

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-08-10

## Context

The game needed a complete first art set — crops at four growth stages, buildings, a character,
animals — in a defined style, with no artist on the project. The conventional path is to model each
asset by hand in Blender and commit `.blend` files.

## Decision

Every asset is produced by Python in `tools/blender/`: a palette module, a builder library, one
function per asset, and a build script that exports GLB and writes a report. The `.blend` is an
output, not a source.

## Consequences

- **Diffable.** `git diff` on an asset shows what changed and why; a `.blend` shows a binary blob.
- **Cannot drift from the style guide, because it IS the style guide.** Palette names, bevel widths
  and triangle budgets are enforced at build time rather than checked in review. Three separate bugs
  were caught this way that review would have missed: a 1,296-triangle barn, an entire building
  family silently rendering grey, and `.001` datablock suffixes about to break name lookup.
- **A palette change propagates to twenty-four assets in one command** instead of twenty-four manual
  edits.
- **Regenerates in under a second**, so the build/review/grade loop is fast enough to actually run.
- **It cannot produce sculpted form.** Facial appeal, cloth, hand-painted texture and animation are
  out of reach. This is the real cost, and it is why "hire an artist for the character rig" is item 9
  of the improvement plan rather than a nice-to-have.
- Procedural repetition is visible on close inspection — assets are recognisably assembled from
  primitives. Acceptable at 20 m; less so in a close-up or a menu portrait.
- Anyone editing the master `.blend` by hand will have their work destroyed by the next build. The
  script is the source; the blend is not.

## Alternatives considered

- **Hand-modelling.** Produces better form and needs an artist and a style-guide review culture the
  project does not have.
- **Purchased asset pack.** Fast, and it would have dictated the art direction rather than serving
  the one chosen from the references, and licence terms would follow the project forever.
- **Generative 3D models.** Output does not respect a palette, a triangle budget, a tile scale or a
  naming convention — every one of which this pipeline enforces mechanically.
